mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as capital flows into equities.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE increasing by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp in 3 months, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strengthening consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS above 3.0%), the Federal Reserve's rate hikes suppress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing output, correlating with strong corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO increases month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL above 260) triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as risk assets face higher discount rates.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 260, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strong labor market, fueling consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (HOUST above 1600), housing market strength indicates economic maturity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as valuation concerns dominate.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (HOUST > 1600), SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
